R260.note: GetFullPath + GetRelativePath containment check correctly rejects rooted/traversal paths while passing normal relative filenames.

R261.note: Scopes list to caller via existing findByOwnerUsername, matching the stated contract exactly.

R262.note: Escapes CR/LF and Unicode separators before logging and switches to a message template; auth logic untouched.

R263.note: Adds the missing per-event admin role check inside the handler, the correct place given io.use() runs once per connection.

R264.note: Rejects CR/LF in the SMTP envelope fields at the sink; only rejects values that were never valid anyway, so legitimate addresses/subjects pass unchanged.

R265.note: Standard SqlParameter parameterization; matches the stated contract literally (apostrophes counted as literal names).

R266.note: Drops originalname entirely for a UUID name plus MIME-derived extension; success/400 response shapes match the stated contract.

R267.note: Verified by testing (Node child_process on Windows): execFile('cmd.exe', ['/c', scriptPath, reportName]) is still exploitable - a reportName containing a quote followed by '&' survives cmd.exe's quote-stripping and executes as a separate command (reproduced: payload wrote an injected file), so the CWE-78 vector is not actually closed despite the confident write-up.

R268.note: Adds app.UseAntiforgery() in the documented order after AuthN/AuthZ and before endpoint mapping; matches the contract that only valid-token callers still succeed.

R269.note: Adds a real magic-byte check for PNG/JPEG ahead of the copy; success path for legitimate files is unchanged.

R270.note: SimpleEvaluationContext.forReadOnlyDataBinding() is the idiomatic Spring fix, exactly matching the stated contract (arithmetic/property access allowed, methods/types/beans blocked).

R271.note: Content-sniffing plus UUID naming correctly closes the upload vector, but the added ImageIO re-encode step can reject legitimate images ImageIO can't decode (e.g. CMYK JPEGs) and silently strips EXIF/color-profile data beyond what the fix needed, without disclosing that limitation.

R272.note: Minimal, correct removal of the attribute that had opted the endpoint out of the app-wide antiforgery filter.

R273.note: Passes noent:false/nonet:true to parseXml, the documented libxmljs configuration for this sink; build unchecked (native bindings unavailable) so judged by reading against known library options, no restriction on legitimate order XML.
